unreg:pitch_velocity_extremes.label: Season maximum pitch velocity thresholds (named pitcher or any pitcher)
unreg:pitch_velocity_extremes.target: Whether a named pitcher, or any pitcher, throws a pitch at or above a velocity threshold (e.g. 107 MPH) in any game of the season including playoffs, per tracked pitch speed.
unreg:pitch_velocity_extremes.mechanism: The season's fastest pitch is the maximum of a bounded per-pitch speed distribution taken over a few thousand near-peak fastballs from a small pool of elite throwers. Exceeding a threshold beyond the tracked record needs a pitcher whose ceiling sits close to it, enough max-effort attempts (relief use, postseason), favourable situations (rest, warmth, leverage), continued health and a tracking reading that lands above the line. The tail is bounded by physiology, so exceedance probabilities beyond the observed record fall off faster than an exponential tail would imply. Covers KXMLBFASTPITCH (named pitcher) and the three KXMLBSTAT velocity events (105+, 106+, 107+ MPH) routed here by the series assignment; the other KXMLBSTAT events belong to season_stat_feats.

unreg:player_and_team_counting_specials.label: MLB postseason league counts (walk-offs, home runs)
unreg:player_and_team_counting_specials.target: Whether the league-wide count of walk-offs, or of home runs by all players, over all games of the 2026 playoffs reaches a threshold.
unreg:player_and_team_counting_specials.mechanism: Postseason league counts are sums over a random number of playoff games of a per-game count. The games remaining come from the bracket path, series lengths and off days; per game, a walk-off needs the home team to bat last while tied or trailing narrowly (skipped bottoms of the ninth, closer deployment, extra innings), and home runs per game come from the two lineups, park, October weather and ball regime with game-shared overdispersion. There is no per-player element, so individual playing time and injury are second order.

attach.why: The any-walk-off definition despite the title, the official recording of home runs and the playoff window come only from the rules wording.
Market-free per-game win probabilities decide series length and so the number of playoff games remaining for both counts.
The designated home-team allocation by round and seed gives home last at-bats, which walk-offs need and home runs do not.
Probability that the home team's bottom of the ninth is skipped removes walk-off exposure from games the home team already leads.
Tie probability entering the ninth and its resolution chain supply the walk-off opportunity states.
Which reliever pitches the ninth by lead size decides the visiting team's hold probability in walk-off states.
Tied-after-nine frequency and postseason extra innings add walk-off chances beyond the ninth.
Ball, pitch clock and extra-innings rule regime shift home-run and walk-off rates and are fixed within a postseason.
October temperature and wind scale home runs per game in the playoff parks.
Ball, pitch clock and rule regime shift strikeout, home-run and starter-length rates between seasons, and so every per-game feat rate.
Series participation, round length and the playoff games distribution depend on which clubs advance; the playoff-games distribution input is computed from the bracket paths.
